decision.rationale: All 19 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping spans Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3). PGS005052 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (Angina pectoris PheCode 411.3), reports a relatively high full-model discrimination metric (C-index 0.7662) plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.491, 95% CI 1.42–1.57), and is from a multi-ancestry evaluation context (AFR/AMR/EUR), which is supportive for robustness. The two strongest runners-up are PGS005048 (highest C-index among listed models at 0.7669 and OR 1.487) and PGS005057 (C-index 0.7664 and OR 1.479). Outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL rather than DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for these top MVP-derived models, making cross-model comparability and PRS-only signal strength less certain; additionally, several near-clone high-performing alternatives are essentially indistinguishable on the visible evidence.

All 19 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported variants include I20 ICD10, PheCode 411.3, and angina/doctor-diagnosed angina). Among the UKB snpnet models from the pan-trait ‘813 traits’ framework (PGS001260/61/62), PGS001262 has the strongest visible PRS-comparable evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.58683 and PGS R² (no covariates)=0.01304, with basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs) and a large European validation (n=49,472). The two best-supported runners-up are PGS001261 (time-to-event angina pectoris) and PGS001260 (angina), which have similar endpoint alignment and comparable PRS-only metrics but slightly weaker PGS-only AUROC/R² than PGS001262. Confidence is not high because the leading UKB snpnet options come from a known pan-trait sparse/framework paper (domain-knowledge penalty for external generalization), while several newer ICD10/PheCode models (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527, PGS00504x–PGS005059) lack PRS-only AUROC/R² and/or have only full-model metrics or ORs, limiting clean cross-candidate comparability in the visible context.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported is angina/ICD10 I20/PheCode 411.3), so a direct-match exists. Among models with PRS-comparable evidence, PGS005048 (MVP; Angina pectoris PheCode 411.3; ldpred; 1,286,612 variants) has the strongest visible effect-size support (OR per SD=1.487, 95% CI 1.41–1.56) alongside a strong full-model discrimination metric (C-index=0.7669) with basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs). Runners-up PGS005052 (OR=1.491, 95% CI 1.42–1.57; C-index=0.7662) and PGS005057 (OR=1.479, 95% CI 1.41–1.56; C-index=0.7664) are extremely similar in endpoint and covariates and have nearly indistinguishable performance, making the top choice not clearly dominant. Confidence is reduced because (i) these MVP models report C-index/full-model rather than explicit PGS-only AUROC/R², and (ii) several near-clone MVP models have essentially tied metrics, so the evidence does not uniquely identify a single best model.

All 19 visible candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported aligns to angina, ICD10 I20, or PheCode 411.3). The strongest direct-match support comes from PGS004527 (I20 angina pectoris) because it reports a moderate-to-strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.429) and is not a pan-trait sparse framework score; however, its performance metrics lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R² and covariates are listed as Unknown, limiting comparability and lowering confidence. As runners-up, PGS005052 and PGS005048 (both PheCode 411.3 angina pectoris) have the highest reported discrimination among the MVP comparative-method set (full-model C-index ~0.766) and strong per-SD ORs (~1.49), but the context does not provide PRS-only metrics and these are from a methods-comparison/portability-style paper with training marked N/A, so their apparent advantage could be partially design/metric-driven. UKB pan-trait snpnet models (PGS001260/1261/1262) provide explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² but are penalized by the domain guidance as pan-trait sparse framework scores and show only modest PRS-only AUROC (~0.58) and small incremental AUROC (~0.008–0.010), making them less compelling despite richer metric reporting.

All 19 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported consistently angina/ICD10 I20/PheCode 411.3). Among them, PGS005052 is best supported by the strongest PRS-discrimination evidence available in the list: it reports a high C-index (0.7663) and a strong per-SD OR (1.491, 95% CI 1.42–1.57) with only basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs) and a reasonably sized European validation (n=30,750) in MVP. The two closest runners-up are PGS005048 (C-index 0.7669; OR 1.487 [1.41–1.56]) and PGS005057 (C-index 0.7664; OR 1.479 [1.41–1.56]); their endpoint and covariates appear essentially identical, and their performance is nearly indistinguishable from the best model.

Limitations keeping this at DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: (1) the MVP set reports full-model C-index rather than an explicitly PRS-only AUROC/R², so comparability across studies is imperfect; (2) several UKB snpnet models (PGS001260/001261/001262) provide explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² but come from a known pan-trait sparse-PRS framework paper (813 traits), and their PRS-only AUROC is modest (~0.58) with small incremental AUROC (~0.008–0.010), making the overall ranking sensitive to study-archetype vs metric-type tradeoffs; and (3) other disease-labeled models (e.g., PGS004527/PGS004457) provide only OR without AUC/C-index and have unknown covariates, limiting direct comparison.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm). PGS000753 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Circulation: “Genetic Architecture of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm in the Million Veteran Program”) and provides a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which is more informative for PRS quality than full-model AUROC alone. Runners-up are the two PRS-CS scores from a large AAA GWAS meta-analysis in Nat Genet (PGS003972/PGS003973), which are also disease-focused and endpoint-aligned; however, their reported discrimination is only via full-model AUROC/C-index (0.69 and 0.882 respectively) with no PGS-only metrics, and the covariate sets differ/are partly unknown, making cross-model comparability limited. Overall confidence is moderate because most candidates lack clearly PRS-only performance metrics (AUC/R2) and two candidates (PGS001784, PGS002054) come from portability/framework-style benchmarking contexts where reported full-model metrics can be less directly interpretable for standalone PRS selection.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis / near-synonymous labels). PGS004913 is best supported because its phenotyping_reported exactly matches the target concept (“Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis”), it is disease-focused, uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and reports PRS-comparable signal (R²=0.029) plus an OR top vs bottom deciles of 4.4. Runner-up PGS001777 is also disease-focused and directly alcohol-related, with a strong risk-gradient metric (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) but is limited by very sparse variants (3), unknown covariates, and a small validation sample (n=1,390), making robustness harder to judge. PGS000704 ranks third despite large validation and a genome-wide model, because the only reported discrimination is a full-model C-index/AUROC (0.711) from a broader biomarker-focused UKB paper; per the domain guidance, full-model AUROC is not a substitute for PRS-only performance, and its modest per-SD HR (1.18) suggests weaker standalone PRS signal. Overall confidence is moderate because none of the candidates provides clean PRS-only AUROC and the reported metrics are not directly comparable across studies.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm). The best-supported direct-match choice is PGS000753 because it is from a disease-focused AAA study (Circulation; Million Veteran Program/MAYO-VDB) with a clean, explicit clinical endpoint (“Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm”), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and it reports a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), providing direct evidence of PRS signal without relying on full-model AUROC. Runners-up: PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a large AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) using genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with extensive disease-focused cohorts; however, their visible performance is only full-model AUROC/C-index with limited PRS-only interpretability and “Unknown”/basic covariate reporting, so they are harder to compare directly. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because across the pool, PRS-only metrics are largely missing or not clearly comparable (several report only full-model AUROC/C-index; one framework/portability score reports covariates-regressed-out R2), leaving meaningful uncertainty in discriminative ranking despite strong endpoint alignment.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with endpoint-faithful phenotyping labels. PGS001777 is best supported because it is explicitly disease-focused for alcohol-related cirrhosis and provides more PRS-relevant signal than the others via a large risk gradient (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) alongside a reported AUROC (0.671) in EUR evaluation. PGS004913 is a close runner-up: it is also disease-focused and endpoint-aligned, reports an OR top vs bottom PRS deciles of 4.4 and an R² of 0.029, but the reported R² is not explicitly PRS-only and the effect estimate is less compelling than PGS001777’s. PGS000704 ranks third despite a large UKB-based development/validation and a genome-wide model, because its only visible discrimination is a full-model C-index (0.711) with covariates (age/sex/PCs), which domain guidance warns is not a substitute for PRS-only performance; its per-SD HR (1.18) suggests only weak-to-moderate PRS signal. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because across candidates the PRS-comparable metrics are limited/heterogeneous (full-model metrics vs effect sizes; no clear PGS-only AUROC/R²), leaving residual uncertainty in cross-model comparability.

All four candidates are direct matches for the target concept via trait_efo/phenotyping (AUD/alcohol dependence measurement). PGS002738 is best supported because it is explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder" and provides a relatively strong, directly interpretable discrimination signal (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a sizable EUR evaluation (n=7,900) and multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB). Runners-up: PGS000201 is closely aligned (DSM-5 AUD criteria count) and reports an incremental ΔR²=0.01192 with a larger variant count and adequate EUR evaluation (n=7,599), but its trait_efo is the less-specific "alcohol dependence measurement" and it lacks OR/HR-style discrimination. PGS002739 remains a direct AUD/alcohol dependence model and reports OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76 (1.32–2.34), but it is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean (AFR) and uses a gene-based PRS-CSx approach with much fewer features, making it less generally supported from the visible evidence for an unspecified target context. Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because no candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R² and covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739, limiting comparability and strength of inference.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder), with PGS002738 and PGS002739 mapping explicitly to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" and PGS000201/PGS000202 mapping to "alcohol dependence measurement" but phenotyping_reported still being DSM-5 AUD criteria count. PGS002738 is best supported because it targets the clinical endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"), is developed in disease-relevant cohorts (MVP, UKB), and reports a relatively strong discriminative effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900). Runners-up: PGS000201 and PGS000202 share the same publication and endpoint (DSM-5 AUD criteria count), use the same method family (PRS-CS) with very large genome-wide variant counts, and provide PRS-contribution metrics (ΔR² vs covariates), with PGS000201 stronger than PGS000202 (ΔR² 0.01192 vs 0.00456; larger validation n=7,599 vs 1,251). Main limitation keeping this as DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: no candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R², covariates are unknown for PGS002738 (reducing comparability), and the remaining candidates measure “problematic alcohol use”/DSM-5 criteria count rather than a clean case-control alcohol dependence definition, making the evidence package incomplete for a clearly high-confidence single winner.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm), so selection hinges on comparative evidence quality. PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) with broad multi-cohort development (many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) and a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS, ~1.1M variants), which domain guidance treats as structurally strong when endpoint fidelity is comparable. However, the available performance evidence is limited/comparability-constrained: the reported AUROC/C-index values appear to be full-model metrics (no explicit PGS-only AUROC), and covariates are listed as unknown, lowering certainty.

Runners-up: PGS003973 is a near-clone sibling from the same Nat Genet study family and method/variant set, with a high reported C-index (0.882) but still not explicitly PRS-only and thus not decisive; it remains strong due to the same disease-focused multi-cohort provenance. PGS000753 is the next best-supported because it is also disease-focused (AAA architecture in MVP) and, unlike most others here, reports an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, moderate signal) which is PRS-informative per domain guidance, though it is a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants and a prevalent endpoint, and lacks AUC/R2.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis / near-synonymous trait_reported and phenotyping_reported). PGS004913 is best supported because it is explicitly disease-focused on alcohol-associated cirrhosis in heavy drinkers, with phenotype-aligned endpoint and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and it reports PRS-comparable signal (R²=0.029) plus an OR top vs bottom deciles of 4.4. PGS001777 is a strong runner-up: also explicitly alcohol-related cirrhosis and reports a large risk gradient (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) and AUROC=0.671, but it is a very sparse 3-variant score, has unknown covariates, and a small validation sample (n=1,390), limiting confidence in robustness. PGS000704 ranks third: it has very large training/validation in UKB and a genome-wide model (183,271 variants; snpnet multi-PRS), but the only reported discrimination is a full-model C-index/AUC=0.711 (not PRS-only), and the publication context is a broad biomarker genetics paper rather than a cirrhosis-focused risk-score study, making the apparent metric advantage less directly interpretable for standalone PRS. Overall confidence is moderate because none of the candidates provides clear PRS-only AUROC and the available metrics are not fully comparable across studies.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned reported/phenotyped endpoints. PGS001777 is best supported on PRS-relevant performance evidence: it reports a strong risk gradient (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) and provides an AUROC (0.671) in a disease-focused context (“genetic risk score … predict development of alcohol-related cirrhosis in drinkers”). Key limitation is that its covariates are listed as unknown and the model is extremely sparse (3 variants), making it harder to judge general polygenic capture and comparability.

Runner-up PGS004913 is also disease-focused and endpoint-faithful (“alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis among heavy drinkers”), with a moderate reported PRS signal (R² = 0.029; OR top vs bottom deciles = 4.4) and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), but lacks an AUROC and has smaller-scale training/validation than the UKB-derived alternative. PGS000704 ranks third: while it has very large UKB training/validation and a genome-wide model (183k variants; snpnet multi-PRS), the only visible discrimination metric is a full-model C-index/AUROC-like value (0.711) with demographic/PC covariates, which domain guidance says is not a substitute for PRS-only performance; its per-SD HR is only modest (1.18), so the PRS contribution is less clearly supported from the visible metadata.

All four listed candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence/AUD), with PGS002738 and PGS002739 mapping exactly to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" and PGS000201/PGS000202 mapping to "alcohol dependence measurement" but with phenotyping_reported explicitly AUD (DSM-5 criteria count). PGS002738 is best supported because it has the most directly aligned trait label ("Alcohol use disorder"), a sizable European evaluation sample (n=7,900), and the strongest visible discriminative evidence among candidates via an OR (top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (95% CI 1.54–2.51). Runner-up PGS000201 remains well supported due to directly relevant phenotyping (AUD DSM-5 criteria count) and the larger incremental ΔR² vs covariates (0.01192) compared with its sibling PGS000202 (0.00456) in the same publication family and similar EUR evaluation context. Second runner-up PGS002739 is a direct-match AUD score with supportive OR evidence (1.76, 95% CI 1.32–2.34) but is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples and uses a much smaller gene-based variant set (858), making it less broadly supported than PGS002738 given the target context provides no deployment ancestry. Overall confidence is moderated by missing PRS-comparable AUC/R² for all models (only incremental ΔR² or ORs are shown) and unknown covariates for PGS002738/PGS002739, which limits comparability.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis). PGS004913 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported explicitly matches alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis) and appears disease-focused (heavy drinkers; GenomALC/NIAAA cohorts) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). It also reports PRS-comparable signal via an R²=0.029 and an OR (top vs bottom deciles)=4.4, giving some standalone PRS evidence beyond full-model discrimination. Key limitation: the reported R² is modest and it is unclear from the visible metadata whether it is strictly PRS-only vs model-dependent, lowering certainty.

Runner-up PGS001777 is also disease-focused and direct-match, with a strong risk-gradient metric (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) and AUROC=0.671, but it is a very small 3-variant score and has unknown covariates plus a small validation sample (n=1,390), which weakens confidence in generalizability. Runner-up PGS000704 has large validation (n=135,300) and a genome-wide model (183k variants; snpnet multi-PRS) with basic covariates, but its publication context is a broad biomarker genetics study and the only visible discrimination is a full-model C-index=0.711 (not a PRS-only metric), with only modest HR per SD (1.18), so PRS-specific performance is less well supported from the provided fields.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence) via trait_efo/phenotyping: PGS002738 and PGS002739 are explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"; PGS000201/PGS000202 report "Problematic alcohol use" but their phenotyping_reported is still AUD (DSM-5 criteria count), making them concept-aligned.

PGS002738 is best supported because it combines a direct alcohol-dependence EFO mapping with an AUD endpoint and provides the strongest visible discriminative evidence among the pool (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96 [1.54–2.51]) on a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=7,900). The main limitation is that covariates are listed as "Unknown" and PRS-comparable AUC/R2 are not reported, reducing comparability and keeping confidence below high.

Runner-up PGS000201 is supported by the same AUD DSM-5 endpoint and shows larger incremental variance explained than its sibling PGS000202 (ΔR² 0.01192 vs 0.00456) with a larger validation sample (n=7,599 vs 1,251) under basic covariates; however, its trait_efo is "alcohol dependence measurement" rather than direct "alcohol dependence".

Second runner-up PGS002739 is also directly mapped to alcohol dependence and reports a supportive OR top 10% vs rest (1.76 [1.32–2.34]) with AFR-only evaluation (n=6,315), but it is less broadly supported for general use in this context due to the different evaluation ancestry versus the other leading EUR-evaluated candidates and limited comparable PRS-only metrics.

All four visible candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence/alcohol use disorder), with strongest endpoint fidelity where phenotyping_reported is explicitly Alcohol use disorder / DSM-5 AUD criteria. PGS002738 is best supported because it is mapped directly to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" and reports a comparatively strong, interpretable validation effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a sizable EUR evaluation (n=7,900) with multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB). The main limitation is that key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R2) are not provided and covariates are listed as Unknown, reducing comparability and certainty.

Runner-up PGS000201 is supported by clear AUD DSM-5 criteria phenotyping and provides an incremental ΔR² vs covariates (0.01192) with a reasonably large validation sample (n=7,599) and basic covariates disclosed; however it is labeled as "Problematic alcohol use" / "alcohol dependence measurement" rather than direct alcohol dependence, and its effect size evidence is weaker than PGS002738’s OR-based stratification signal.

Second runner-up PGS002739 is also a direct alcohol dependence EFO match but is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean ancestry (n=6,315), making it less generally supported in the current context (which does not specify a target deployment ancestry). It has a solid OR top 10% vs rest (1.76, 95% CI 1.32–2.34) but uses a much smaller, gene-based variant set (858) and has Unknown covariates, leaving more uncertainty. Overall confidence is Moderate because multiple direct-match candidates exist and none reports PRS-only AUC/R², so ranking relies heavily on effect-size summaries and endpoint alignment rather than fully comparable discrimination metrics.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent but still same disease endpoint). Among them, PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.12M variants), which is structurally favored for polygenic traits versus sparse P+T, and is not a pan-trait portability sweep. Its reported discrimination is only a full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates, so PRS-only comparability is limited—this is the main reason the overall outcome is not high-quality. Runner-up PGS003973 is a sibling from the same Nat Genet study family (same method/variant count, similar endpoint) but its reported metric is a full-model C-index (0.882) with basic age/age^2/sex covariates; because this is not PRS-only and is not directly comparable across models, it is supportive but discounted. The second runner-up PGS000753 is disease-focused (Circulation; MVP/Mayo; reports OR per SD 1.37 [1.30–1.44]) but uses a very sparse P+T score (29 variants), which is structurally weaker than the PRS-CS genome-wide models despite having an interpretable PRS effect size. Framework-style candidates (PGS001784 global biobank; PGS002054 UKB portability) are deprioritized despite having PRS-comparable R2/partial-r (~0.014–0.0147), because domain guidance warns such framework scores typically underperform disease-focused models when direct disease-focused alternatives exist, and their reported AUROC/R2 evidence here remains modest and/or not clearly PRS-only AUROC.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent but still aligned). Best-supported pick: PGS003972 is from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) using genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with a large variant set, which is structurally favored for polygenic traits; it also reports a full-model AUROC=0.69 (not PRS-only) with EUR evaluation. Main limitation: reported discrimination is not PRS-only/comparable (no PGS-only AUROC/R2/OR per SD), and covariates are listed as Unknown, reducing comparability and confidence.

Runner-up 1 (PGS003973): same disease-focused Nat Genet study family and same method/variant count with EUR evaluation; reports a high full-model C-index=0.882, but this is likely covariate-driven (covariates include Age/Age^2/Sex) and is not PRS-only, so it is discounted per the provided domain guidance; otherwise it remains a strong direct-match sibling.

Runner-up 2 (PGS000753): exact AAA endpoint (prevalent AAA) and provides a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD=1.37, moderate) plus basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), but it is an older sparse P+T score with only 29 variants, which is structurally weaker than genome-wide shrinkage models when other evidence is similar.

Other direct-match candidates were ranked lower: PGS001784 and PGS002054 come from framework/portability-style papers (Cell Genom global biobank PRS; AJHG portability of 245 scores) and their reported PRS-comparable metrics (R2 ~0.014–0.0147 / partial-r 0.0144) are modest; PGS003429 is a screening cost-effectiveness context with unknown covariates and only full-model metrics, offering limited standalone PRS evidence.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (ankylosing spondylitis) by trait_efo/trait_reported, with generally coherent phenotyping_reported (except one time-to-event variant). For best_model_id, PGS001267 is preferred because it provides the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence in this list (explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.7265 and PGS-only R2=0.0988, plus full-model AUROC=0.7433 with only basic covariates) and has endpoint-fidelity consistent with the generic target (phenotyping_reported: Ankylosing spondylitis). The main limitation is that it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused efforts, lowering confidence.

Runners-up: (1) PGS001268 is a near-clone from the same framework family with slightly higher reported AUROC/R2, but its phenotyping_reported is explicitly time-to-event (TTE ankylosing spondylitis), which domain guidance treats as a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic disease-risk target; thus it ranks behind PGS001267 despite similar/stronger metrics. (2) PGS002089 is a direct ankylosing spondylitis score with a methodologically strong genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2; 22,026 variants) and a higher reported partial correlation (0.0919) than the sibling penalized-regression portability score (PGS001876 partial-r=0.0797), but it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 and comes from a UKB portability framework context, making the performance evidence less directly comparable than for PGS001267/PGS001268.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo, with generally good phenotype alignment except PGS001268 which is explicitly time-to-event (a mild endpoint mismatch for generic disease-risk use per domain guidance). PGS001267 is best supported because it reports PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.7265) and PGS-only R² (0.0988), plus full-model AUROC with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), enabling clearer cross-model interpretation than candidates that report only partial-r or only full-model AUROC. Runner-up PGS001268 has very similar, slightly higher reported metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.7346; PGS-only R² 0.1023) but is time-to-event, which the domain knowledge flags as a warning signal unless outweighed by stronger disease-focused evidence (not present here since both are from the same pan-trait UKB framework family). The second runner-up is PGS002089 because, among the remaining non-time-to-event case-control scores, it has the strongest available PRS-quality signal reported (partial correlation 0.0919 with CI) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with many variants (LDpred2; 22,026), whereas the Taiwanese EAS-only models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (not PRS-comparable) and the other UKB portability sibling (PGS001876) has weaker partial-r (0.0797). Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the top two candidates come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (explicitly cautioned in the domain knowledge as often less robust externally), and several other direct-match candidates lack PRS-only comparable metrics or have unknown covariates, limiting certainty.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo, and most also by phenotyping_reported. Among them, PGS001267 is best supported in this context because it provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.7265) and PGS R2 (no covariates, 0.0988), plus full-model AUROC (0.7433) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a large European validation sample (n=67,425). PGS001268 is a close runner-up with slightly higher PRS-only AUROC (0.7346) and R2 (0.1023) but has a time-to-event phenotype (TTE ankylosing spondylitis), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic disease-risk target per the provided domain guidance. For the second runner-up, PGS002089 is preferred over other remaining candidates because it is endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported: ankylosing spondylitis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with many variants (22,026), and reports a stronger PRS-comparable partial correlation (0.0919) than PGS001876 (0.0797), though both lack AUROC/R2 and come from a portability framework study. Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS000327, PGS002790) with trait_reported/trait_efo aligned to autism spectrum disorder. All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity and comparability. PGS002755 is the best-supported direct-match because its reported endpoint is incident atopic dermatitis (well-aligned to generic atopic eczema risk), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants; structurally strong for a polygenic trait), and it reports a PRS-associated HR (high vs low PRS) with CI in a very large European evaluation (n=337,910). The main limitation is that no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so effect-size evidence is limited to a single HR contrast and cross-model metric comparability is weak.

Runners-up: PGS004587 also targets incident atopic dermatitis and reports a similar HR with CI in the same large European evaluation size, but it is a sparse genome-wide-significant SNP score (23 variants), which is structurally weaker than PRS-CS for a polygenic disease and offers no clearer performance advantage. PGS001773 is a direct atopic dermatitis score but is restricted to moderate-to-severe disease in Canadian cohorts and reports only full-model AUROC/R2 (0.93/0.49) with demographic/ethnicity covariates; per domain guidance, full-model AUROC is not a substitute for PRS-only performance and the very high values raise concern that discrimination is largely covariate-driven and/or not comparable. The remaining candidates (PGS003459, PGS003486, PGS004903) are therapy-specific ‘paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis’ endpoints, which are poorer matches to generic atopic eczema risk despite being eczema-labeled.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (atopic eczema). Ranking is driven primarily by endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported) and then by the strength/comparability of available performance evidence.

Best: PGS002755 is a clean direct match with an incident atopic dermatitis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: incident AD) and a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants). It reports a modest but interpretable PRS association (HR high vs low PRS = 1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a very large European evaluation sample (n=337,910). Limitations: no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so comparative discrimination cannot be directly assessed; reported HR is not per-SD and is only one type of metric.

Runner-up 1: PGS004587 has the same incident AD endpoint and the same large European evaluation sample size (n=337,910), with an HR high vs low PRS = 1.153 (1.037–1.282). It is structurally weaker (23 SNP genome-wide significant set) and shows a weaker effect size than PGS002755, but remains endpoint-faithful.

Runner-up 2: PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (a subtype/restriction vs generic atopic eczema) and reports a very high full-model AUROC (0.93) and R² (0.49), but these are full-model metrics with multiple non-genetic covariates (including parental ethnicity) and are not PRS-only; the magnitude is also implausibly high as PRS-comparable evidence relative to the provided heritability ceiling guidance, so it is heavily discounted. Still, it is disease-focused and directly aligned to atopic dermatitis, so it remains a plausible runner-up over the therapy-specific ‘paradoxical eczema in psoriasis treated with biologics’ models (PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903), which have explicit endpoint mismatch for generic atopic eczema.

All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter) by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable evidence and study archetype. PGS005168 (Nat Genet 2025 meta-analysis) has strong direct phenotype alignment (atrial fibrillation), appears disease-focused with many contributing cohorts, uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), and reports strong discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) plus an HR~1.67, making it the best-supported direct-match option in the visible set. Runner-up PGS005313 (Nat Commun 2025) is also disease-focused and uses PRS-CSx with strong reported AUROC 0.78 and OR 1.82, but has less extensive visible validation support (single record shown) and evaluation context details are less clear than for PGS005168. Runner-up PGS000016 (Nat Genet 2019) is a clean direct AF score with LDpred and reports PRS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.029 (a PRS-comparable metric consistent with the provided AF heritability ceiling) plus large validation n, but its reported discrimination is weaker/older relative to the newer disease-focused meta-analysis evidence. Confidence is Moderate because many candidates report only full-model metrics or are packaged with clinical risk calculators/horizon-specific endpoints (e.g., CHARGE-AF, 5-year risk), making cross-model metric comparability uneven even though PGS005168 remains the most coherently supported.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to autism spectrum disorder), but only one has clean endpoint fidelity. PGS002790 is a weaker runner-up despite a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (SDPR) and very large variant count, because its phenotyping_reported is 'Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)', which is an explicit endpoint mismatch/ambiguity relative to ASD diagnosis; its reported metric is only partial R²=0.00546 with no effect sizes shown, making PRS-comparable performance evidence both weaker and less directly tied to ASD. Overall confidence is limited (no PGS-only AUC/R² for either model, and PGS000327’s R² appears to be a full-model metric), so the direct-match recommendation is present but not high-certainty.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the ontology level (trait_efo includes atopic eczema). Ranking is driven primarily by endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported) and then by the comparability/strength of reported PRS evidence.

Best: PGS002755 (Atopic dermatitis; phenotyping_reported: incident atopic dermatitis) has a clean, generic disease incidence endpoint aligned to the target trait, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants), and reports a moderate HR (high vs low PRS) of 1.249 (95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a large EUR evaluation (n=337,910). Lower-ranked direct matches: PGS003459, PGS003486, and PGS004903 are all primarily about paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis patients (therapy/context-specific endpoint), which is a weaker match to generic atopic eczema risk despite having atopic-eczema labeling.

All highlighted candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation by trait_reported/trait_efo, so ranking is driven by endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported), PRS-comparable evidence, and study archetype/covariate cleanliness per the provided domain_knowledge. PGS005168 is best supported because it is a disease-focused AF meta-analysis PRS (Nat Genet; multi-cohort training_development_cohorts list) with a direct AF endpoint (phenotyping_reported: atrial fibrillation), basic-plus-clinical-risk adjustment that is explicitly flagged as not heavy leakage in the guidance (age/age^2/sex/PCs/array plus CHARGE-AF), and strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) alongside a strong per-SD effect size signal (HR 1.6663). Runner-up PGS005313 is also a disease-focused, multi-cohort AF score with strong effect size (OR 1.82 with tight CI) and reported AUROC 0.78 with only basic covariates (age, sex), but it is evaluated in a non-EUR-only setting (EVAL: MAE 100%) and has less extensive visible validation detail than PGS005168. Third, PGS000331 (Nat Med) remains a strong older disease-focused multi-cohort incident AF model with basic covariates and supportive effect size (HR 1.62) and C-index 0.751, but it is less compelling than the two newer multi-cohort AF-specific models given the weaker reported discrimination and no PRS-only metrics.

All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF+flutter) by trait_reported/trait_efo and generally compatible phenotyping. All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter), so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity, PRS-comparable evidence, covariate comparability, and study archetype. All three candidates are direct-match on concept/ontology (bipolar disorder / bipolar I / bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), training cohort (PGC), and EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, so the differentiating evidence is weak. Overall confidence is low due to the phenotype/endpoint mismatch signals and lack of PRS-only performance metrics.

All three candidates are direct matches via trait_efo including the target (bilirubin metabolism disease). PGS001824 and PGS002032 have the tightest endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: “Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), whereas PGS000924 uses a broader composite endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism (time-to-event)”), which is a partial endpoint mismatch plus a time-to-event framing (a warning signal in the provided domain guidance). Between the two bilirubin-excretion models, visible performance evidence is limited to the same modest partial correlation (partial-r=0.0716) with no PRS-only AUROC/R² reported for either, and covariates are similar; therefore method/structure becomes the main differentiator. Penalized regression (bigstatsr) in PGS001824 is selected over LDpred2 in PGS002032 only weakly from the visible metadata (no head-to-head PRS-comparable metrics to confirm superiority), so confidence is moderate and the overall outcome is sub-optimal due to missing comparable discrimination metrics for the leading candidates and the framework/time-to-event concerns for the remaining alternative.

All three candidates are direct-match to the target trait axis (bipolar disorder spectrum) via trait_reported/trait_efo: PGS002786 (bipolar disorder), PGS002787 (bipolar I disorder), PGS002788 (bipolar II disorder). However, endpoint fidelity is a major limitation for all three because phenotyping_reported is not a direct bipolar diagnosis endpoint (it references cognition/psychiatric behavior measures), making the models’ evaluation context potentially misaligned with the target disease-risk use. PGS002786 is preferred because it matches the umbrella target label (bipolar disorder) most directly, while PGS002787 and PGS002788 are reasonable runners-up as clinically adjacent subtype scores but remain similarly limited by the non-diagnostic phenotyping field.

All three candidates are direct matches via trait_efo including “bilirubin metabolism disease”. PGS002032 and PGS001824 have the most endpoint-fidel phenotyping (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”) matching the target EFO exactly, whereas PGS000924 targets a broader composite (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”) and is time-to-event, which is a mild endpoint penalty per the provided domain guidance. Between the two bilirubin-excretion siblings from the same publication/family with identical reported partial-r (0.0716) and similar ancestry/covariates, PGS002032 is structurally preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far higher variant count (19,768 vs 22), which is a positive signal when other evidence is otherwise indistinguishable. Main limitation: for PGS002032 and PGS001824, standard PRS-comparable AUC/R² (including PGS-only metrics) are not reported, leaving only partial correlation and making the ranking less certain; PGS000924 reports unusually high AUROC/R² but is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper and has a broader TTE endpoint, so that performance evidence is discounted and does not clearly outweigh the endpoint/method concerns.

All visible candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_efo and (mostly) phenotyping_reported. All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept (trait_efo includes/equals “bilirubin metabolism disease”). PGS002032 is preferred because it has the most endpoint-faithful and specific phenotype among the set (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion” in both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with a large variant set (19,768), which is a positive structural signal for polygenic traits when comparable PRS-only metrics are not available. PGS000924 is ranked third despite reporting high apparent AUROC/R² because it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”), has a time-to-event composite endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism (time-to-event)”) rather than the specific bilirubin-excretion disorder, and its very high full-model AUROC is not a substitute for missing PRS-only comparability per the provided domain guidance.

All 20 listed candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). For best-model selection, endpoint fidelity and comparable performance evidence dominate. PGS000452 has a clean, direct endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), EUR development/evaluation, and is among the strongest on the visible validation metrics in this list (full-model AUROC 0.632; Nagelkerke R² 0.0487; per-SD OR 1.663; top-1% vs rest OR 3.61). Two close runners-up from the same coherent Cancer PRSweb family are PGS000454 (same endpoint/covariates/ancestry; full-model AUROC 0.632; Nagelkerke R² 0.0489; per-SD OR 1.661; top-1% vs rest OR 3.79) and PGS000456 (same endpoint/covariates/ancestry; full-model AUROC 0.63; Nagelkerke R² 0.0456; per-SD OR 1.633; top-1% vs rest OR 3.95). Confidence is Moderate because none of the candidates report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so rankings rely on full-model metrics and effect sizes; additionally, several near-clone PRSweb models are extremely close on reported performance, making fine ordering somewhat unstable from the visible metadata alone.

All three candidates are direct matches via trait_efo including “bilirubin metabolism disease.” The two exact-endpoint models (PGS002032, PGS001824) have the highest phenotype alignment: trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are both “Disorders of bilirubin excretion,” directly mapping to the target disease concept. Between these two near-clones from the same publication (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”), reported performance evidence is effectively identical (same partial-r=0.0716 with similar CIs; no PRS-only AUROC/R2 reported), so structural signals dominate: PGS002032 uses genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2) with far more variants (19,768) than PGS001824 (22 variants, penalized regression), which is supportive for a polygenic architecture when other evidence is indistinguishable. PGS000924 is a broader/partially different endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism (time-to-event)”) and comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk; although it reports high AUROC/R2, its PRS-only R2 (0.218) exceeds the provided local heritability sanity estimate (h2_obs≈0.089), creating unresolved comparability concerns. Overall, a direct match exists, but confidence is limited by missing comparable PRS-only discrimination metrics for the top two candidates and the near-tie between them.

All visible candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_reported/trait_efo. Ranking therefore leans on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported), then comparable performance evidence (effect sizes; noting full-model AUROC is not PRS-only), with transportability/method as secondary. PGS000452 is best supported because it has an exact BCC endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest reported discrimination signals among the MGI PRSweb sibling set (full-model AUROC 0.632 with relatively high Nagelkerke R² 0.0487 and strong per-SD OR 1.663; top-1% vs rest OR 3.61). The two closest runners-up are PGS000454 (nearly identical endpoint/covariates with essentially the same AUROC 0.632 and slightly higher R² 0.0489 and similar per-SD OR 1.661) and PGS000456 (same endpoint/covariates with AUROC 0.63, R² 0.0456, per-SD OR 1.633), all from the same publication family and evaluation ancestry (EUR). Confidence is Moderate rather than High because these top candidates are near-ties with very small differences, and the reported AUROCs are full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), limiting cross-model comparability and making fine-grained ranking uncertain.

All 20 visible candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). For best-model selection, endpoint fidelity and comparable performance evidence dominate. All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO concept (bilirubin metabolism disease), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS002032 and PGS001824 are the most phenotype-aligned: both target 'Disorders of bilirubin excretion' with trait_efo exactly 'bilirubin metabolism disease' and identical partial-r performance evidence (0.0716 in EUR validation). Between them, PGS002032 is preferred on structural grounds because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (19,768 vs 22), which is generally favored for polygenic architectures when endpoints and metrics are otherwise indistinguishable. However, confidence is limited because neither model reports PRS-comparable AUROC or PRS-only R², and the only reported metric is partial correlation, making the overall strength of evidence modest.

PGS000924 is a broader/partially composite endpoint ('Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism (time-to-event)') and comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet; 813 traits paper), which domain guidance flags as prone to poorer external generalization; it also has an extremely small variant count (5). Although it reports high AUC/R² and PGS-only metrics, these appear inconsistent with the provided local heritability ceiling context for bilirubin (~0.089) and are therefore treated cautiously as potentially non-comparable or scale-mismatched in this setting, so it ranks behind the two endpoint-faithful portability-study scores.

All three candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches to the target bipolar disorder spectrum (bipolar disorder, bipolar I, bipolar II) and share the same publication (Transl Psychiatry, 2022-09-29), method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, and similar genome-wide variant counts (~935k–949k), so there is no clearly dominant model on structural grounds. Endpoint fidelity is a major limitation: each model’s phenotyping_reported reflects cognition/behavior traits (e.g., pattern comparison; DSM5 depression; sluggish cognitive tempo) rather than a direct bipolar disorder diagnosis endpoint, which weakens direct-match support per the provided domain guidance. With no PRS-comparable AUC/PGS-only metrics and only small partial R² values reported (full_model_r2 ~0.0025–0.0031) in modest validation samples (~2.2k–2.5k), the evidence is insufficient to strongly prefer one model. PGS002786 is selected as best only because it is the broadest disease label match (bipolar disorder rather than subtype) while otherwise being near-identical to its siblings; runners-up are PGS002787 and PGS002788 (subtype-specific labels) with similarly limited and non-diagnostic phenotyping evidence.

All three candidates are direct matches at the level of the target umbrella concept (blood coagulation disease), but they differ in endpoint specificity and evidence quality. PGS002034 and PGS001826 both target a specific coagulation disorder subtype (congenital deficiency of vitamin K–dependent clotting factors) with consistent trait_reported/phenotyping_reported alignment; between these near-clones from the same publication (UKB portability framework), PGS002034 is structurally preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45) while showing essentially identical reported partial-r (~0.056) and similar ancestry/validation context. PGS001826 is the closest runner-up given the same endpoint and nearly identical performance evidence but weaker structural properties. PGS001033 is a broader ‘other coagulation defects’ time-to-event endpoint and is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet) with an extremely sparse 1-variant model; despite having explicit AUROC fields, the framework+sparsity and TTE endpoint lower confidence for generic deployment. Overall confidence is only moderate because the best-supported candidates (PGS002034/PGS001826) come from a portability/framework paper with limited comparable discrimination metrics (partial-r only; no PGS-only AUROC/R²), and the third candidate’s reported AUROC is not sufficient to overcome its sparse framework characteristics.

All three candidates are direct matches at the umbrella level via coagulation-disorder endpoints, but each has notable limitations. PGS002034 and PGS001826 are the most phenotype-aligned to a specific coagulation disease entity (both: “Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”; EFO: congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency), whereas PGS001033 targets a broader/less specific endpoint (“Other coagulation defects” with a time-to-event phenotype). Between the two congenital-deficiency siblings from the same publication and with essentially identical covariates, ancestry context, training cohort (UKB), and very similar partial-r, PGS002034 is preferred on structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 32,552 variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants), which domain knowledge treats as a moderate positive signal when other evidence is near-indistinguishable. However, confidence is only Moderate and the overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because (i) performance reporting for PGS002034/PGS001826 is limited to partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R²), and (ii) all candidates come from framework-style UKB analyses (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”; “across 813 traits…”), which domain knowledge flags as generally less reliable for external generalization than disease-focused multi-cohort models—none of which are present here to resolve that limitation.

All three candidates are direct matches at the broad target level (“blood coagulation disease”) via either the exact EFO mapping (PGS001033) or a closely related coagulation-defect diagnosis (PGS001826/PGS002034: congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency). The strongest within-list support is for PGS002034 because it has high endpoint fidelity (explicit congenital clotting-factor deficiency phenotype) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with substantially more variants (32,552) than its near-clone sibling PGS001826 (45 variants), which is a positive structural signal when other fields are essentially identical (same publication family, cohorts, covariates, training size, and very similar partial-r). PGS001826 is the best runner-up as the closest sibling with the same endpoint and nearly identical reported partial-r, but it is structurally less informative due to far fewer variants and a penalized regression sparse model. PGS001033 is ranked third despite having explicit AUROC/R2 fields because it is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits…”) and is extremely sparse (1 variant) with a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are warning signals for external generalizability; additionally, its reported AUROC evidence is not clearly PRS-only (full-model AUROC is present and domain guidance discourages over-weighting full-model AUROC). Remaining limitation: none of the top-ranked congenital-deficiency models provides standard PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 in the visible metrics (only partial correlation), and the target trait is broader than the congenital deficiency endpoint, so confidence cannot be high.

All three candidates are direct matches at the target’s disease-family level via coagulation-defect endpoints, but all come from high-throughput UK Biobank framework papers (a known generalization weakness in the provided domain guidance), so none is clearly high-quality. PGS001033 is preferred because it maps to the target EFO term (blood coagulation disease), provides the clearest endpoint field for this target in-context (“TTE other coagulation defects”), and is the only candidate with explicit discrimination metrics reported (including PGS-only AUROC and PGS-only R²) alongside only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). The main limitation is that it is a very sparse snpnet model (1 variant) from a pan-trait UKB framework and uses a time-to-event phenotype, both of which lower confidence in external robustness. As runners-up, PGS002034 and PGS001826 share the same reported congenital clotting-factor-deficiency endpoint and publication/covariates; PGS002034 is ranked above PGS001826 on structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 32,552 variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants) with essentially identical partial-r performance reported, leaving PGS001826 as the third choice.

All three visible candidates are direct matches at the broad level (all map to the coagulation-disease space), but none is strongly supported because two lack standard PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (AUC/R²) and the remaining one is a pan-trait sparse UKB framework score with an extremely low variant count.

Best (PGS002034): Chosen because its phenotype/trait is a specific coagulation disorder endpoint (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”) and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a large variant set (32,552), a structural positive signal when performance metrics are otherwise limited. It also reports a partial correlation (partial-r 0.0563, EUR validation) providing at least some comparable performance evidence.

Runner-up 1 (PGS001826): Same endpoint, same publication family, similar partial-r (0.0562) and validation context; ranked below PGS002034 primarily due to much smaller variant count (45) and a less structurally strong method choice relative to LDpred2, with no other differentiating evidence visible.

Runner-up 2 (PGS001033): Has explicit AUROC/PRS-only AUROC fields available, but the score is from a pan-trait “813 traits in UK Biobank” sparse framework (snpnet) and is effectively non-polygenic here (variants_number=1) with a time-to-event phenotype label, both warning signals for external reliability; therefore it is deprioritized despite having more complete AUC reporting.

Main limitation: the top two candidates (PGS002034/PGS001826) provide only partial-correlation metrics (no AUC/R²), and all candidates are UKB-derived framework/portability contexts rather than clearly disease-focused multi-cohort coagulation studies, keeping confidence below high.

Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant in the visible list. Among the highest-supported cluster, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV; phenotype: Breast cancer; covariates: 0) has the strongest reported full-model discrimination in its directly comparable family (AUROC 0.6625) plus strong effect-size evidence (OR 1.83 per SD) and variance explained (R² 0.0764), all with an endpoint-faithful breast cancer phenotype and no covariate packaging beyond genetics.
